quarterly_data.signal: Relay's 10-K FY2025 results: research and development expenses were $261,383 thousand versus $319,089 thousand in 2024, general and administrative expenses $56,710 thousand versus $76,592 thousand, and net loss $276,479 thousand versus $337,708 thousand. Cash, cash equivalents and investments were $554.5 million as of December 31, 2025, which Relay believes will fund operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into 2029. All of its product candidates are in development and none has received marketing approval in any jurisdiction.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D $261,383 thousand (2025) vs $319,089 thousand (2024); G&A $56,710 thousand vs $76,592 thousand; net loss $276,479 thousand vs $337,708 thousand; cash $554.5 million; runway into 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Relay's 10-K on pipeline and supply: it expects zovegalisib to compete against Piqray (alpelisib, Novartis), Truqap (capivasertib, AstraZeneca) and Itovebi (inavolisib, Roche through Genentech), and names Eli Lilly and OnKure as running mutant-selective PI3Kα programs; its non-inhibitory chaperone for Fabry disease is expected to compete against Galafold (migalastat, Amicus Therapeutics) and the enzyme replacement therapies Fabrazyme (Sanofi), Replagal (Takeda) and Elfabrio (Protalix Biotherapeutics). All drug candidates are small molecules made by third-party contract manufacturers, and the API, drug product and starting materials are supplied primarily from single-source suppliers with no redundant or second-source supply in place.
